items.title: The 5 Phases of a Project Management Plan

source_refs.note: Unnumbered topic The 5 Phases of a Project Management Plan (PDF 16-17, printed 13-14). The figure shows only the phase names; the one-line explanations of each phase are general project-management meaning and are flagged for review.

blocks.text: A project management plan moves through five phases.

items: Initiation: the project idea is defined and approved.
Planning: tasks, people, timelines and costs are worked out.
Execution: the team does the work and builds the product.
Performance monitoring: progress, cost and quality are checked against the plan.
Project closure: the finished product is handed over and the project is closed.

blocks.alt: Top left: five boxes for the project phases, initiation to closure, with notes on planning, timelines, costs, the cost example and risk steps. Top right: a use case diagram of a library system with a librarian and a student linked to Borrow book and Return book. Bottom: a class diagram with Room, Box and the ToyBox, BookBox and ClothesBox classes.
blocks.caption: Project planning, risk management, use case and class diagrams (original diagram after Figures 1.9 and 1.10 and the planning topics).
blocks.long_description: A project passes through initiation, planning, execution, performance monitoring and closure. Its plan sets what will be done, by whom and when, and its cost depends on the team, the technology, the duration, the risks and quality assurance; risks are identified, analysed, mitigated and monitored. A use case diagram shows the people or systems outside a system, such as a librarian and a student, and the goals they reach with it, such as borrowing and returning books. A class diagram shows classes with their data and actions and how they are related: a room holds boxes, and toy, book and clothes boxes are special kinds of box.
